subject: Delta Health — Renewal: rightsizing & surge-proofing dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@deltahealth.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Delta Health Procurement <procurement@deltahealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + recent spikes — need recommendations

Hi Neha,

We’re starting renewal conversations internally and wanted to flag a couple of operational surprises from Q3. Between Aug 14–Sep 02 we saw two sustained burst windows that pushed our sustained concurrency from 320 -> ~540 for several hours; that drove token costs way up and caused a handful of degraded latencies on critical endpoints.

Our current Dedicated commitment (H100-slab, 120 GPUs reserved) renews in late November. Before we sign another 12-month commitment the CTO and SRE want a concrete plan for:
- Rightsizing based on observed utilization (do we shrink reserved count or shift to a hybrid of reserved+burst?)
- A safety/buffer approach to avoid SLA hits during short surges (hot-standby vs. burst credits vs. slice rebalancing)
- Estimated delta in monthly unit cost for each option

Can you and the team run a short analysis and propose 2–3 clear options with numbers and a recommended path? We’d like that ahead of our internal renewal review next week. If possible, include any short-term mitigations we can enable while contract terms are finalized.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Ops, Delta Health

Subject: Re: Renewal planning + recent spikes — need recommendations

Samira — thanks for the clear note and the heads-up on the timing. I pulled the Q3 telemetry and attached a short CSV (usage_report_Q3.csv) showing per-hour concurrent requests, median latency, and model mix during the spike windows.

Plan: we’ll propose three discrete options (conservative, efficiency-first, and hybrid surge-proof). Karthik will map the workload to hardware options and outline latency impacts; Ben will provide cost/contract implications and a renewal term scenario for each.

Short-term mitigation (can enable within 48 hours): 1) enable prefix KV caching for the top 12 routes (we estimate ~18% token reduction in the burst window); 2) temporarily allow controlled model-mix fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant for low-priority background jobs to reduce pressure on H100 slots. Those are operational toggles we can apply immediately.

I’ve cc’d Karthik and Ben — expect a consolidated note by tomorrow EOD with numbers and a recommended path. If you have a preferred time for a 30-min sync next week, send a couple slots and we’ll lock it.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Samira / Neha — ran a quick pass on the Q3 telemetry and modeled three technical pathways. Attaching a short scenario deck (safety_pool_scenarios.pdf) with the math. TL;DR: expected latency and cost tradeoffs per option below.

Option A — Conservative top-up
- Add +40 H100 reserved GPUs (160 total) to match 95th percentile peak headroom.
- Pros: simplest to operate, minimal code changes, predictable latency.
- Cons: higher committed cost (~+24% monthly).
- Estimated latency change: none (same model mix).

Option B — Slice rebalancing + quantized fallbacks (recommended for cost/latency balance)
- Repartition reserved pool: keep 120 H100 reserved; repack 12 GPUs worth of capacity into a small L40-style pool for background/async jobs; shift non-critical workloads to an 8-bit/4-bit quantized model variant.
- Add a 12-GPU hot-standby buffer (burst pool) on pay-as-you-go for SLO-protected endpoints during 1–4 hour surges.
- Pros: reduces committed spend, improves unit economics; burst pool handles the short spikes without expanding the long-term commit.
- Cons: requires validation of quantized model quality for non-critical paths; small operational complexity for routing.
- Estimated monthly delta: ~+6% to committed spend (for a small standby + burst usage) but overall token costs drop by ~14% due to caching+quantized reduction.
- Latency impact: median latency for critical endpoints unchanged; background jobs see slightly higher p95 during fallback but within tolerance.

Option C — Minimal reserve + larger burst credits
- Drop reserved to 100 GPUs, rely on larger burst credits (pre-purchased or on-demand) to handle spikes.
- Pros: lower fixed commitment, flexible.
- Cons: risk of capacity contention in extreme events; higher per-token cost during bursts.
- Estimated monthly delta: -12% committed cost but +25% in burst token expense if bursts are frequent.

Next steps: tell us which option you want priced (we’ll output month-by-month cashflow and a 12-mo comparison). I’ll also sketch an implementation checklist for Option B if you want to pilot it by Nov 1.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Samira — I priced the three options against your current ARR/commit. Summary below; full line-item numbers are in the attached draft MA (deltahealth_ma_draft.docx) and I’ve pushed a deal record to HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEL-2026-1083

Option A — Conservative top-up
- Incremental cost: +$72k/mo committed (12-mo term); 24% increase to committed spend.
- Estimated one-time onboarding / capacity re-provisioning credit: $10k (we can include 50% credit for a 12-mo sign).

Option B — Slice rebalancing + quantized fallbacks (recommended)
- Incremental cost: +$18k/mo for the small hot-standby + burst baseline (keeps long-term commit ~flat).
- One-time migration validation / model QA credit: $8k.
- We can extend a 7% committed discount if you sign a 12-mo term with an explicit SLO uplift (0.5% tighter p95).

Option C — Minimal reserve + larger burst credits
- Net committed reduction: -$36k/mo (if you move to 100 GPUs).
- Expect higher variable spend: projected +$45k/mo in peak months if bursts repeat.

Contract mechanics: I can attach an amendment with the Option B baseline (we’ll include a 60-day review clause to measure actual burst frequency and adjust the reserve up or down). I’ve included a draft DocuSign envelope link in the attachments for when you’re ready.

Ask: please confirm which option you want us to finalize and I’ll circulate the amendment + DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
